Subject: Slot-trade & cloud backstop for Neptune dedicated pool

Hey Rachel / CloudBridge / John —

Quick framing: Neptune's renewal is asking for a dedicated pool sized ~120 A100-equivalent GPUs on Redwood Dedicated, target onboarding window Sep–Oct 2027. Omega's current Q3 manufacturing slot queue is tight; Rachel mentioned a potential slot-trade (move Neptune one tranche earlier in exchange for a price uplift / deposit) which could materially reduce lead time risk for us.

We'd like to scope a concrete mutual-action plan that combines:
- OEM slot-trade options (what you can commit to and cost)
- CloudBridge backstop offering (short-term burst capacity for onboarding/QA)
- A timeline that ties to Neptune's contract milestones so we can sign deals with confidence

Ask: Rachel, can you send a succinct slot quote + earliest committed ship date for a tranche of ~40 GPUs (we're open to split tranches) and the terms for a slot-trade? CloudBridge, can you share a short SOW and hourly/weekly rates for a 12-week backstop pool and lead time to stand that up? John — I copied you so you see the options we plan to present; any hard cutover date constraints from Neptune's side?

Attachments: I will drop our current Neptune run-rate and target SLA in a follow-up if helpful.

Thanks — aiming to have numbers by EOD Tue so we can propose a combined fallback to Neptune in Wednesday's commercial touchpoint.

— Priyom

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can offer a slot-trade for a 40-GPU tranche that moves Neptune into our earlier Q3 manufacturing window, conditioned on a 30% non-refundable deposit and a slot-trade fee (one-time) of $45k for expedited scheduling. Committed ship ETA if deposit received by 2027-05-10: 2027-08-28 (container departure).

Details attached: omega_slot_quote_Q3-2027.pdf — includes per-unit pricing in the trade scenario, FOB port, and our cancellation/reschedule windows. Notes:
- We can split into two 40-GPU tranches (totaling 80) and leave remaining capacity to later tranches if Neptune wants staged onramp.
- Lead time after deposit is fixed in our schedule; any changes trigger a requeue fee.

We can do a brief sync tomorrow to walk the terms if helpful.

Best,

Team — quick internal recap and options to present to Neptune:

1) Take the slot-trade for one 40-GPU tranche now:
   - Cost: 30% deposit (per Rachel) + $45k trade fee.
   - Outcome: ship ETA 2027-08-28, reduces risk for Sep onboarding.

2) Staged OEM + Cloud backstop:
   - OEM provides two 40-tranche windows (we accept first tranche, second later).
   - CloudBridge stands up a 12-week backstop pool for onboarding/load testing at an estimated cost of $X/hr (~attachment forthcoming).
   - This avoids forcing Neptune to accept full upfront spend on hardware if they prefer phased commitment.

3) Pure cloud backstop (no slot-trade):
   - Higher variable cost, but faster to start; worst-case higher TCO and potential performance/value differences.

Concerns: finance — deposit exposure and treatment under our reserved capacity contracts; Ops — staging/transfer plan for KV caches and model weights if we move from CloudBridge to Redwood Dedicated (data migration window and expected downtime).

Can Ben/Karthik comment on the finance/ops tolerance for the deposit + trade fee? Lauren, can you flag any procurement/legal hooks we should expect if Neptune requests an amendment to the term sheet to cover deposits and delivery guarantees?

If we align, I'll draft a short two-option proposal to Neptune: (A) Slot-trade + modest backstop for ramp; (B) Cloud-only rapid onramp with longer-term procurement cadence.

— Priyom

Thanks — my quick read:

- Finance: Deposit is acceptable if we treat it as a refundable credit against Neptune's committed reserved capacity (i.e., deposit becomes credit on contract signature within 90 days). If Neptune refuses conversion, we should push for a smaller deposit or escrow mechanism. Ben — confirm net cash exposure limits for this deal (I remember a $250k threshold for exec signoff).

- Ops: CloudBridge backstop is sensible, but we must document the migration runbook (expected time to sync cached models and warm KV cache). Recommend we require CloudBridge to deliver network peering and snapshot export formats in the SOW.

- Commercial ask: ask Omega to include a modest SLA on delivery windows or a liquidated-damages clause tied to major slips; it'll help Neptune feel comfortable.

If everyone agrees, Priyom, go ahead and propose option A (slot-trade + 6-week CloudBridge backstop) with an alternative B (cloud-only ramp). I can help draft the contract language re deposit-credit.

— Karthik

Rachel / CloudBridge / John — thanks for the quick turnaround and helpful details. Short proposal to align before we present to Neptune: 

Option A (preferred):
- Omega provides 40-GPU slot-trade with deposit = 30% (credited to Neptune on contract signature within 90 days) + $45k trade fee. Committed ship ETA 2027-08-28.
- CloudBridge provides a 6-week backstop pool (reduced from 12 weeks) for onboarding/testing; SOW to include network peering, snapshot/export capability, and support for KV cache warm-up. Estimated cost: see attached SOW (cloudbridge_backstop_SOW_v3.docx).
- Redwood to manage migration plan and acceptance criteria for Neptune cutover.

Option B (fallback):
- No OEM deposit. Cloud-only onramp with a 12-week backstop and staged conversion to Dedicated when OEM slots become available.

Next steps: Rachel — can you confirm acceptance of the deposit-as-credit wording and add a one-paragraph SLA on delivery windows (or proposed liquidated-damages verbiage) by EOD Thu? CloudBridge — please confirm SOW acceptance and a firm turnaround (we need an operational lead and stand-up ETA). John — if Neptune has any constraints on the escrow/credit treatment, let us know before Thu EOD so we can bake it into the commercial.

If we get these confirmations, we'll package Option A into a one-page appendix to include with the Neptune commercial proposal on Wednesday's executive review.

Thanks all,
